ph.lead: I help organisations identify sustainable solutions, players and partners in Europe that fit their goals – and turn the findings into usable knowledge, meetings and practical progress. The service can be a focused scan, opening contacts, a meeting programme, an expert study trip or a combination of these.
ph.scope: I work across Europe. My strongest base of projects, experience and networks is in Germany, the rest of the DACH region and the Netherlands. The overarching theme is sustainability in the broad sense: for example energy and environmental solutions, the circular and bioeconomy, biodiversity, social sustainability, and sustainable food and tourism.

brief.title: Benchmark Brief – background and insights in one place
brief.p1: An expert study trip can include a concise Benchmark Brief. It brings together the trip's theme, the most interesting solutions and players, background on the sites visited and the key questions for comparison in an easy-to-use format.
brief.p2: The brief helps participants prepare for the meetings and, after the trip, supports shared discussion, decision-making and follow-up.
price.q: What does a group trip cost?
price.p1: The cost of a group trip can be covered through project or other funding, split into per-participant fees, or invoiced to the client in full.
price.p2: The price always follows the content and the way the trip is delivered. It depends on the length of the trip and the destination area, the size of the group, the number of site visits, meals and other programme, and whether I travel with you as tour leader. On request, travel logistics — flights, accommodation and coach transfers — can be included as well; the full travel package is then provided by the travel agency partner I work with.
price.figure: Ballpark €1,200–1,800 + VAT / participant On the three-day trips to Central Europe delivered so far, the total cost has typically been at this level, with travel logistics and my tour leadership included.
price.figure.description: price — text. Contains HTML markup (e.g. <em> or <strong>). Keep the tags as they are and change only the text between them.
price.p3: Every trip is nevertheless planned as its own package. The right way to deliver it, the content and an initial budget frame are gone through together already in the first conversation.

p4.title: Summarising and working on the lessons
p4.lead: A scan, meetings or an expert study trip can be the start of longer-term development. Where needed, I help the group gather the key findings, identify shared conclusions and define concrete next steps.
p4.desc: This can take the form of a facilitated summary discussion, small-group work or a compact workshop as part of a scan or trip.

pwhy.title: Encounters that land, lessons that last.
pwhy.lead: At its best, what a trip yields keeps paying off long after everyone has gone home. Five things set the work apart.
pwhy.1.title: A grasp of the subject
pwhy.1.desc: I can connect the themes and find the one site that is genuinely worth visiting. Sustainability, energy, the circular economy and the environment are the core of my work.
pwhy.1.desc.description: Why FinDera section, item 1 — body text.
pwhy.2.title: Opening doors
pwhy.2.desc: I secure meetings with the right people and with the right agenda.
pwhy.2.desc.description: Why FinDera section, item 2 — body text.
pwhy.3.title: Reliable delivery
pwhy.3.desc: A rhythm that works, realistic logistics, smooth running and good group dynamics.
pwhy.3.desc.description: Why FinDera section, item 3 — body text.
pwhy.4.title: A multi-stakeholder view
pwhy.4.desc: It comes from a career spanning the private sector, the public sector and central government.
pwhy.4.desc.description: Why FinDera section, item 4 — body text.
pwhy.5.title: Tour leadership and a good atmosphere
pwhy.5.desc: Smooth execution, good spirit, and a trip participants remember.
pwhy.5.desc.description: Why FinDera section, item 5 — body text.
pwhy.note: The hardest work and the real risk are not in the itinerary on paper. They are in the quality of the sites, in getting the meetings confirmed, in a rhythm that holds, and in whether the visits genuinely serve the objective. Get those right and the trip produces insights, contacts and concrete next steps.
